title: Blocking On Retries
eyebrow: Design question · design loop fixes (parent issue #457) · asked during Build by the #460 builder

short.lead: Your pick 2A said the decided-for-aj check blocks a reply until it links a page, up to three blocks in a row. The builder for #460 (Decided-for-aj check) found that the plugin cannot do that today, and stopped to ask rather than choose. The end-of-reply check blocks a reply once. When I send the reply again (a retry), it only reports, and it never blocks (hook.py:123). The three-in-a-row limit exists only as an unused number (design_loop.py:1984), and the check's own message wrongly says a missing page keeps blocking. The same question decides #461 (Page check blocks again for choices and decisions).
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it changes and what it needs from you.
items: hook.py lines 194-199 run the blocking checks only on the first try. On a retry, every check only reports.
How hard should these two checks hold?
Your pick sets how #460 and #461 are built.
#465 (Rerun limit counts reading a script as running it) does not depend on this answer.

choices: How should the decided-for-aj check and the page check block?
Block on retries too, up to three in a row

Only these two checks may block a retry. After three blocks in a row the reply goes through with a note naming what is missing, so a broken page builder cannot loop a session with nobody watching. Every other check keeps today's once-only rule. The check's message is corrected to match.
Block once, like the other checks
The reply is blocked once. If my retry still settles a point without a page, it goes through with a report. Simpler, but a second try can get past it, which is how decisions slipped through before.
Block on every retry, with no limit
Strictest. A false match on harmless wording, or a broken page builder, would stop the session until you step in.
A matches the three-block limit you chose for the page rule in #283, and it is the only option where a retry cannot simply walk past the check.

wrapup.summary: The decided-for-aj check and the page check need permission to block a retry, which no check has today. One pick decides both.
wrapup.changing: Nothing until you answer. #465 is being built meanwhile.
wrapup.next: Your answer goes into #460 and #461, and the builder for #460 resumes.
